qadi.s: A qadi is a judge in Islamic law, responsible for applying sharia in civil, family and criminal cases. Qadis were appointed by Muslim rulers from the Rashidun and Umayyad caliphates onwards.

qadiriyya.s: The Qadiriyya is one of the oldest and most widespread Sufi orders in Islam, named after the twelfth-century scholar Abd al-Qadir al-Jilani. Usman dan Fodio, founder of the Sokoto Caliphate, belonged to the order.

qahtanites.s: The Qahtanites are the Arabs who traced their descent from the legendary ancestor Qahtan, associated with southern Arabia and Yemen. In the Umayyad period the Yemeni or Qahtani tribal faction was bitterly opposed to the northern Arab Qays.

qajar-capture-of-shiraz.s: The Qajar capture of Shiraz was the taking of the Zand capital by Agha Mohammad Khan Qajar in 1791. According to the site it completed the formal dissolution of the Zand Empire.

qajar-dynasty.s: The Qajar dynasty was a Turkmen dynasty that ruled Iran from the late eighteenth century until 1925. Its founder Agha Mohammad Khan defeated the Zand Empire and in 1796 took Mashhad, ending the last remnant of the Afsharid Empire.

qalawun.s: Qalawun was a sultan of the Mamluk Sultanate in the late thirteenth century and founder of a dynasty that ruled for about a century. His campaigns continued the work of Baybars against the Crusader states and the Mongols.

qanat.s: A qanat is an underground channel that carries water by gravity from mountain aquifers to lowland fields and settlements. The technique originated in ancient Iran and spread across arid regions.

qapaghan-qaghan.s: Qapaghan Qaghan was a ruler of the Second Turkic Khaganate from 691 to 716. He was its leading military commander, crossing the Yellow River repeatedly to force tribute from the Tang and conquering the Yenisei Kyrgyz in 710.

qara-khitai.s: The Qara Khitai, or Western Liao, was a Central Asian state founded in the twelfth century by Khitan refugees from northern China after the fall of the Liao dynasty. It defeated the Seljuk sultan Ahmad Sanjar at the Battle of Qatwan in 1141, destroying Seljuk Empire authority…

qarmatians.s: The Qarmatians were a radical Ismaili movement based mainly in eastern Arabia and Bahrain from the late ninth century. They raided widely and famously seized the Black Stone from Mecca in 930.

qarshi.s: Qarshi is a city in southern Uzbekistan, in the region of Transoxiana. In the 1320s Kebek Khan of the Chagatai Empire attempted to make it a stable sedentary capital.

qays.s: The Qays were the northern Arab tribal grouping that opposed the Yemeni or Qahtani faction in the early Islamic period. Their rivalry dominated the politics and armies of the late Umayyad period.

qazi.s: Qazi is the form of the Arabic word qadi, meaning a judge in Islamic law, used in Persian and South Asian contexts. In the Delhi Sultanate qazi courts administered sharia as the formal legal framework of the state.

qianlong-emperor.s: The Qianlong Emperor ruled the Qing Empire from 1735 to 1796, presiding over its greatest territorial extent. His Ten Great Campaigns conquered Dzungaria and Eastern Turkestan and reached into Burma, Vietnam and Nepal.

qin-dynasty.s: The Qin dynasty was the first imperial dynasty of China, which unified the country in 221 BCE under Qin Shi Huang. It standardised writing, weights and measures and created a centralised bureaucratic state.

qing-conquest-of-taiwan.s: The Qing conquest of Taiwan took place in 1683, when Qing naval forces under Shi Lang defeated the Kingdom of Tungning ruled by the descendants of Koxinga. The island had been the last stronghold of Ming loyalist resistance.

qing-empire.s: The Qing Empire was the last imperial dynasty of China, founded by the Manchus, who conquered Ming China from 1644 and ruled until 1912. It expanded China's territory to include Mongolia, Xinjiang and Tibet and presided over great population and commercial growth.

qiniq.s: The Qiniq were a clan of the Oghuz Turks of Central Asia. Seljuk Beg, the eponymous ancestor of the Seljuk dynasty, was a chieftain of the Qiniq who converted to Sunni Islam around 985 CE.

qizilbash.s: The Qizilbash were a confederation of Turkmen tribes devoted to the Safavid Sufi order, named after their distinctive red headgear. They brought Ismail I to power in 1501 and formed the core military and political elite of the Safavid Empire.

quanzhou.s: Quanzhou is a port city in Fujian province in south-eastern China. Under the Song Dynasty it was one of the busiest ports in the world, linking China with South-east Asia, India, the Persian Gulf and East Africa.

quchan.s: Quchan is a town in Khorasan in north-eastern Iran. Nader Shah, founder of the Afsharid Empire, was assassinated by his own officers near Quchan on 20 June 1747.

quebec.s: Quebec is a city on the St Lawrence River in Canada. Samuel de Champlain founded it in 1608 as the capital of New France and the centre of the fur trade.

queen-of-sheba.s: The Queen of Sheba is a figure from biblical and Quranic tradition who visited King Solomon. Ethiopian tradition, codified in the Kebra Nagast, holds that she bore Solomon a son, Menelik, founder of a royal line.

quelimane.s: Quelimane is a port town on the coast of Mozambique, near the Zambezi delta. In the eighteenth century gold and ivory from the Zimbabwean plateau reached the coast through Quelimane and Sofala.

quinquereme.s: A quinquereme was a large ancient warship powered by oarsmen arranged in groups of five per vertical unit. It was the standard battleship of the Hellenistic and Punic navies.

quintus-fabius-maximus.s: Quintus Fabius Maximus was a Roman statesman and general during the Second Punic War. After Hannibal's early victories he adopted a strategy of avoiding pitched battle and wearing down the Carthaginian army, earning the name Cunctator, the delayer.

quran.s: The Quran is the central religious text of Islam, believed by Muslims to be the word of God revealed to the Prophet Muhammad. Under the caliph Uthman of the Rashidun Caliphate its text was standardised into a single authoritative recension.

quraysh.s: The Quraysh were the dominant Arab tribe of Mecca, to which the Prophet Muhammad belonged. Its Umayyad clan initially opposed Muhammad before his victory in 630 CE.

qurchi-bashi.s: The qurchi-bashi was the commander of the qurchis, the royal guard of Qizilbash cavalry, in the Safavid Empire. The office was one of the most powerful in the central administration, commanding the Qizilbash military establishment.

qut.s: Qut is an Old Turkic concept of heavenly charisma or good fortune, believed to be granted by the sky god Tengri to a legitimate ruler. Possession of qut justified a qaghan's authority over the steppe peoples.

qutb-minar.s: The Qutb Minar is a tall minaret of red sandstone in Delhi, begun around the end of the twelfth century under Qutb ud-Din Aibak and completed by his successors. It stands within a complex that includes one of the earliest mosques in India.

qutb-ud-din-aibak.s: Qutb ud-Din Aibak was a Turkic slave-general of the Ghurid ruler Muhammad of Ghor, who governed Delhi as viceroy from 1192. After his master's death he declared himself independent ruler, founding the Mamluk or Slave Dynasty.

qutuz.s: Qutuz was a sultan of the Mamluk Sultanate in 1259–1260. With the general Baybars he led the Mamluk army that defeated a Mongol force under Kitbuqa at Ain Jalut in Galilee in 1260.
